body.estimand_functional: \([\min_{q\in\Theta(P)}Q_{q,T}(P,\rho,b,o,e),\max_{q\in\Theta(P)}Q_{q,T}(P,\rho,b,o,e)]\), with one stationary response-mass vector shared across every date and hidden branch

sampling_model.design: One stationary iid-response SCM generates the factual record; an independent generative calibration experiment supplies rowwise multinomial draws.
sampling_model.units: The causal query concerns one unit observed for \(T\) transitions; calibration units are independent across draws and rows.
sampling_model.treatment: The factual and alternative interventions are the fixed stationary policies \(b\) and \(\pi\).
sampling_model.overlap: Known nominal support with \(P(y\mid x,a)\ge\epsilon\) on each positive cell; no response-program mass is bounded away from zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The controlled transition law is either known or estimated by \(\widehat P\) from independent rowwise multinomial calibration samples; no trajectory-only nuisance estimator is claimed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 4.1--4.3 give exact closed-form lower and upper bounds for one counterfactual transition after one observed transition.
Theorem 2.4, Proposition 2.5, and Theorem 2.8 reduce finite discrete counterfactual bounds to optimization over a complete canonical SCM family.
The average-reward results derive concentration for one fixed policy and kernel from a Poisson-equation martingale decomposition.
In the paper's special casino model, the time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous \(\mathrm{EWAC}/T\) bounds converge together as \(T\to\infty\) (arXiv version 3, pages 9--11, Sections 4.2--4.3).
The paper constructs uniformly asymptotically valid confidence intervals for smooth projections of moment-identified parameter sets.
The paper generates individual POMDP counterfactual trajectories after selecting the Gumbel-Max SCM and proves its counterfactual-stability property.
The paper gives exact polynomial-program bounds for a terminal counterfactual probability in a dynamic latent-state model with time-invariant response distributions.
Theorems 2 and 4 control martingale-process suprema through sequential Rademacher complexity and sequential covering integrals.
Section 2 represents causal mechanisms as implicit couplings, while Propositions 1--2 establish limitations of fixed implicit couplings.
Theorems 12.8 and 14.7 derive self-normalized maximal and vector-martingale inequalities by exponential mixing.
Uniform observability guarantees nonlinear-filter stability without stability assumptions on the hidden signal.
The paper derives forgetting of an HMM filter from explicit coupling conditions on posterior kernels.
Section 5 gives an efficient influence function and an efficient asymptotically normal estimator for worst-case value under multiplicative transition perturbations.

body.tldr: A known finite controlled transition law does not identify the same unit's counterfactual trajectory because it leaves the response-program coupling unspecified. The closest long-record comparator shows only that, in a special casino model, time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous \(\mathrm{EWAC}/T\) bounds converge together as \(T\to\infty\); it gives neither a finite root-\(T\) rate nor a bound uniform over the complete finite-state stationary response-program fiber. Under the explicitly induced factual law \(\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}\), the field-level kernel asks whether the expected diameter of the sharp coarsened-record average-reward interval contracts at the root-\(T\) rate uniformly over that complete fiber, without positive response masses or contraction of conditional counterfactual kernels. The first D0 obligation is the synchronizer--two-permutation square: it must yield a uniform two-parameter root-\(T\) bound or an explicit horizon-dependent counterselection with the sharp replacement rate. Only an affirmative square-to-polytope maximal inequality activates the conditional \(1024B d^{dk}/(\epsilon\sqrt T)\) width theorem. A stationary shared-response endpoint proposition supplies infrastructure, while a full-support root-\(T\) lower witness and simultaneous finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage complete the proposal.

project_justification.gap: Published SCM work supplies selected-mechanism trajectories, exact one-step compatible-coupling bounds, or generic finite canonical programs. The closest long-record result, HaughSingal2026Casino, shows only that in its special casino model the time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous \(\mathrm{EWAC}/T\) bounds converge together as \(T\to\infty\). It gives neither a finite root-\(T\) rate nor a bound uniform over the complete finite-state stationary response-program fiber, while average-reward concentration supplies a Poisson martingale only for one fixed kernel.
project_justification.niche: The missing field-level object beyond that qualitative special-casino limit is a finite-horizon uniform maximal inequality for posterior-normalized Poisson martingales indexed by the complete response polytope, including zero-mass faces and noncontracting conditional kernels. The synchronizer--two-permutation square is the decisive first interior-face test.
project_justification.fill: The project first resolves that square by a uniform root-rate bound or a sharp horizon-dependent counterselection, then conditionally propagates an affirmative bound to the whole finite-state stationary response-program polytope and an explicit finite root-\(T\) expected-width theorem. This directly supplies the rate and uniformity absent from the special-casino asymptotic comparison. Full-record and coarsened-record functionals are kept separate under \(\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}\); stationary endpoint attainment, a full-support lower construction, and simultaneous calibration-set inversion are supporting components.

body.related_work: HaughSingal2026Casino, arXiv version 3, pages 9--11, Sections 4.2--4.3, is the closest long-record comparator: in its special casino model, the time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous \(\mathrm{EWAC}/T\) bounds converge together as \(T\to\infty\). That qualitative special-model conclusion gives neither a finite root-\(T\) rate nor a bound uniform over the complete finite-state stationary response-program fiber studied here. LallyKazemiPaoletti2026RobustCounterfactualMDP, Section 4 and Appendix D.1, replaces arbitrary mechanism selection by sharp compatible-SCM optimization, but its one-transition results do not analyze one stationary response law after a long record. ZhangTianBareinboim2022PartialCounterfactual, Theorem 2.4, Proposition 2.5, and Theorem 2.8, supplies generic finite canonical-SCM optimization; the stationary shared-response endpoint proposition here is supporting infrastructure, not a claimed improvement over that result. HaughSingal2023DynamicLatent uses time-invariant response distributions for a terminal probability-of-necessity program after a complete record, but proves no contraction rate in record length. SayedanaCainesMahajan2025, Lemma 67 and Theorems 17--18, supplies the fixed-kernel Poisson telescoping move; the unresolved step here is a supremum over posterior-conditioned response laws under \(\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}\). deLaPenaLaiShao2009 informs the predictable-scale route, and RakhlinSridharanTewari2015, Theorems 2 and 4, informs sequential-complexity control, but neither evaluates the nonlinear response-filter family at vanishing response masses. OberstSontag2019 and LorberbomJohnsonMaddisonTarlowHazan2021 explain why a known MDP law does not select a level-three mechanism, but both choose or learn one coupling rather than report the full compatible interval. KaidoMolinariStoye2019CalibratedProjection motivates projection of a covered nuisance region; the confidence theorem instead uses exact rowwise multinomial coverage and deterministic fiber inclusion. vanHandel2009 and DoucMoulinesRitov2009 study posterior stability within a fixed hidden model; the coarsening lemma compares full-record and coarsened-record envelopes without importing their stability assumptions. BennettKallusOprescuSunWang2024RobustOPE treats multiplicative transition perturbations and an unconditional policy value, rather than response-coupling ambiguity for a same-unit conditional counterfactual.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The verified presolve argument currently yields only \(O(\sqrt{\log T/T})\) over the whole response polytope and \(180/\sqrt T\) on the union of the twenty-eight binary antipodal segments. Edgewise control does not imply control of interior mixtures. The synchronizer--two-permutation square in \texttt{def:triangle-handle} is the first D0 obligation: it must produce a uniform two-parameter root-\(T\) bound or an explicit horizon-dependent counterselection and sharp replacement rate. A proof that assumes conditional positivity does not address the stated class.
body.honest_scope: The root-\(T\) whole-polytope inequality and its explicit constant are open, so \texttt{thm:root-t-width} is only an implication from an affirmative resolution of \texttt{oeq:polytope-maximal-inequality}. D0 must first decide the synchronizer--two-permutation square; failure requires replacing the headline with the sharp rate supported by a legal horizon-dependent sequence on that face. The stationary shared-response endpoint proposition is supporting infrastructure rather than a generic polynomial-optimization novelty claim. The Poisson decomposition, binary lower witness, and multinomial union-inversion architecture have presolve support but remain statements to prove. Claims are in expectation at fixed horizon, not recordwise or anytime. Absorbing target chains with class-dependent reward averages are excluded because they admit no scalar-\(g\) Poisson solution. Date-specific response laws are excluded because rectangular datewise coupling can keep the width equal to one.
